recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If the work group wants the older Jira resolution wording cleaned up, handle that as Jira cleanup or separate human review; no FHIR-core source change is needed for FHIR-36093.
issue_request: FHIR-36093 reported that the R4 VitalSigns.category slicing by value:coding.code and value:coding.system prevented derived profiles from allowing alternate codings in a category slice. It is Applied, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification for R6; the original resolution text said to change category:VSCat.coding to 1:1, but later Jira comments clarified that the issue was already handled by changing to pattern:$this slicing and that the literal 1:1 change would be wrong.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-36093 was found. The applicable source change appears in git 71babbf5ac for FHIR-46418, which changed Observation.category slicing from value:coding.code/value:coding.system to pattern:$this and replaced fixed VSCat.coding child constraints with a VSCat patternCodeableConcept. FHIR-46418 already has its own combined-branch audit commit.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini, the Vital Signs IG is marked core in source/igs.xml, and source/observation/implementationguide-Observation-vitalsigns.xml includes StructureDefinition/vitalsigns. A 2022 Zulip thread confirmed the fixed repeated coding behavior that motivated FHIR-36093, and later FHIR-44798 narrative now explicitly says additional category codes may be included with the vital-signs category code. 2025 OO minutes raised whether to reopen FHIR-36093 because the literal resolution did not appear applied, but Jira remains Applied and the source implements the behavior described in the later Jira comments.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source has Observation.category sliced with open pattern:$this rules, VSCat expressed as a patternCodeableConcept for the vital-signs coding, and no Observation.category:VSCat.coding child element that would require every coding to match vital-signs.
